name: German Sauerbraten
description: Sauerbraten, one of Germany's official national dishes, genuinely depends on a marinade of several days, sometimes up to a week or more, in vinegar, wine, and aromatics - real sources are explicit not to cut corners here, since the length of the marinade is what tenderizes the meat and builds the dish's real sour character; this version is honestly abbreviated for practicality, disclosed rather than pretending an overnight soak is traditional. Real technique dissolves crushed gingersnap cookies into the strained braising liquid, which both thickens the gravy and balances its sourness with real sweetness.
steps_detailed: Combine the vinegar, wine, onion, carrot, bay leaf, and cloves, and marinate the beef in this mixture at least 24 hours, ideally longer if time allows - real sauerbraten traditionally marinates for several days to a week.
Remove the beef, pat dry, and brown well, 8-9 minutes.
Strain the marinade, reserving the liquid, and add it back to the pot with the sugar.
Simmer 1.5-2 hours until the beef is completely tender.
Stir in the crushed gingersnaps and simmer 8-10 minutes more, until they dissolve and thicken the gravy into a real sweet-and-sour sauce.

name: German Schnitzel (Jägerschnitzel)
description: Jägerschnitzel, 'hunter's schnitzel', is a real breaded cutlet topped with a genuine mushroom cream sauce, real technique frying the schnitzel first and keeping it warm while the sauce comes together separately, so the breading stays crisp.
steps_detailed: Dredge the pounded chicken in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Fry in the oil, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden, then set aside, keeping it warm.
In the same pan, cook the onion 3-4 minutes, then add the broth and cream, and simmer 5-6 minutes until slightly thickened.
Spoon the sauce over the schnitzel just before serving, so the breading stays crisp.

name: German Pretzel (Brezel)
description: Brezel, the real Bavarian soft pretzel, depends on a genuine baking soda or lye-water dip before baking, which is what gives it its distinctive deep mahogany crust and slightly chewy texture.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and baking powder with warm water into a firm dough. Rest 15 minutes.

Dip briefly in a solution of the baking soda dissolved in hot water - real technique depends on this real alkaline dip for the distinctive dark, chewy crust.
Sprinkle with salt and bake at 425F (220C) for 15-18 minutes until deeply browned.
